objects.description: Abstract byte sink interface in snappy namespace. Provides virtual Append plus buffer acquisition helpers for efficient appends. Non-copyable; ownership and lifetime defined by subclass. Default implementations of buffer helpers may return caller-provided scratch. Destructor is virtual and defined elsewhere.

Abstract byte source interface in snappy namespace. Supports querying available bytes, peeking a contiguous region without advancing, and skipping bytes. Non-copyable. Destructor is virtual and defined elsewhere.

Concrete Source that reads from a contiguous byte array. Maintains a pointer and remaining-length counter. No bounds checks beyond contract; user must ensure buffer lifetime exceeds this object’s lifetime.

Concrete Sink that writes sequentially to a caller-provided flat buffer without bounds checking. Caller must ensure sufficient capacity and that dest_ remains valid. Provides fast append and buffer acquisition; exposes CurrentDestination() to inspect write pointer.

Forward declaration of an abstract byte source used by the snappy APIs to read compressed or uncompressed data. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the actual definition is elsewhere.

Forward declaration of an abstract byte sink used by the snappy APIs to receive compressed or uncompressed data. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the actual definition is elsewhere.

Options controlling snappy compression behavior. Currently only exposes a compression level (1 or 2). Provides constexpr ctor, range helpers, and default level. Fully defined here and used by several overloads of Compress/RawCompress APIs.
Enumeration of return statuses for the Snappy C API. Values indicate success, invalid/corrupt input, or insufficient output buffer size. Used as the return type of all functions in this header.

functions.name: snappy::Sink::Sink
functions.description: Constructs a Sink interface object. This base class consumes a sequence of bytes via Append and related helpers. Intended to be subclassed.
requirements: Must only be instantiated directly if providing a concrete subclass (Sink is abstract due to at least one pure virtual function).

functions.name: snappy::Sink::~Sink
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Sink. Enables safe deletion via a base-class pointer.

functions.name: snappy::Sink::Append
functions.signature: void snappy::Sink::Append(const char* bytes, size_t n) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual: append bytes[0..n-1] to the sink. Implemented by concrete Sink subclasses.
requirements: bytes must point to a buffer containing at least n bytes.
May be called with n == 0; behavior for bytes == nullptr is unknown if n > 0 (not documented).
Must only be called on a valid, initialized Sink instance.

functions.name: snappy::Sink::GetAppendBuffer
functions.description: Returns a writable buffer of the requested length for appending. The returned buffer is valid only until the next operation on this Sink. After writing at most length bytes, the caller must invoke Append() with the same pointer and the number of bytes actually written. Default implementation always returns the scratch buffer; implementations may return an internal buffer to avoid copies. If a non-scratch buffer is returned, only a prefix may be passed to Append (no interior pointers).
requirements: scratch must point to a caller-owned buffer of at least length bytes.
Caller must write no more than length bytes to the returned buffer.
Caller must subsequently call Append(returned_pointer, bytes_written) with bytes_written <= length before any other Sink operation.
If a non-scratch buffer is returned, the caller may only pass a prefix of that buffer to Append (must not pass an interior pointer).
Returned buffer becomes invalid after the next operation on this Sink.

functions.name: snappy::Sink::AppendAndTakeOwnership
functions.signature: void snappy::Sink::AppendAndTakeOwnership(char* bytes, size_t n, void (*deleter)(void*, const char*, size_t), void* deleter_arg)
functions.description: Appends bytes[0..n-1] to the sink, taking ownership of the buffer and freeing it by calling deleter(deleter_arg, bytes, n). Default implementation calls Append() then frees bytes; optimized sinks may avoid a copy.
requirements: deleter must be non-null.
bytes must point to a buffer of at least n bytes that can be released using the provided deleter.
Ownership of bytes transfers to the sink; the caller must not read or free bytes after calling this function.
Must only be called on a valid, initialized Sink instance.

functions.name: snappy::Sink::GetAppendBufferVariable
functions.signature: char* snappy::Sink::GetAppendBufferVariable(size_t min_size, size_t desired_size_hint, char* scratch, size_t scratch_size, size_t* allocated_size)
functions.description: Returns a writable buffer for appending and writes its capacity to *allocated_size (guaranteed >= min_size). May return scratch (caller-owned) or an internal buffer. The returned buffer is valid only until the next operation on this Sink. After writing at most *allocated_size bytes, the caller must invoke Append with the same pointer and number of bytes written. If a non-scratch buffer is returned, only a prefix may be passed to Append. desired_size_hint may be 0 if unknown; implementations may use it to size allocations.
requirements: scratch must point to a caller-owned buffer with scratch_size >= min_size if it is to be used.
allocated_size must be non-null and writable; on return, *allocated_size >= min_size.
Caller must write no more than *allocated_size bytes to the returned buffer.
Caller must subsequently call Append(returned_pointer, bytes_written) with bytes_written <= *allocated_size before any other Sink operation.
If a non-scratch buffer is returned, the caller may only pass a prefix of that buffer to Append (must not pass an interior pointer).
Returned buffer becomes invalid after the next operation on this Sink.
desired_size_hint may be 0 if the caller cannot provide a reasonable guess.

functions.name: snappy::Source::Source
functions.description: Constructs a Source interface object. This base class yields a sequence of bytes via Peek and Skip. Intended to be subclassed.
requirements: Must only be instantiated directly if providing a concrete subclass (Source is abstract due to pure virtual functions).

functions.name: snappy::Source::~Source
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Source. Enables safe deletion via a base-class pointer.

functions.name: snappy::Source::Available
functions.description: Pure virtual: returns the number of bytes left to read from the source.
requirements: Must only be called on a valid Source instance.

functions.name: snappy::Source::Peek
functions.description: Pure virtual: peek at the next flat region without advancing. Returns a pointer to the beginning of the region and stores its length in *len. The region is valid until the next call to Skip() or until the object is destroyed. The region size may exceed Available(); the caller must only read Available() bytes.
requirements: len must be a non-null pointer to writable memory.
Caller must not read more than Available() bytes from the returned region.
Any buffer returned by a previous Peek() is invalidated after Skip() or destruction of the Source.

functions.name: snappy::Source::Skip
functions.description: Pure virtual: skip the next n bytes and invalidate any buffer returned by a previous Peek().
requirements: Requires Available() >= n at the time of the call.
Invalidates any buffer previously returned by Peek().
Must only be called on a valid Source instance.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::ByteArraySource
functions.description: Constructs a Source that yields the contents of a flat byte array p of length n.
requirements: p should point to a contiguous array containing at least n bytes (inferred from the class purpose).
The memory referenced by p must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the ByteArraySource (inferred).

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::~ByteArraySource
functions.description: Destructor for ByteArraySource.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::Available
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes remaining in the underlying array.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::Peek
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the next contiguous region in the underlying array and stores its available length in *len without advancing. Region remains valid until Skip() or destruction. May return a region larger than Available(); callers must only read Available() bytes.
requirements: len must be non-null and writable.
Caller must not read more than Available() bytes from the returned region.
Any buffer returned is invalidated by a subsequent call to Skip() or object destruction.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::Skip
functions.description: Skips the next n bytes in the underlying array and invalidates any region returned by a previous Peek().
requirements: Requires Available() >= n at the time of the call.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::UncheckedByteArraySink
functions.description: Constructs a Sink that writes to a caller-provided flat array starting at dest without performing any bound checks.
requirements: dest must be a valid, writable pointer to sufficient storage for all data that will be appended (no bounds are checked).
The memory pointed to by dest must remain valid and writable for the lifetime of the sink or until writing is complete.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::~UncheckedByteArraySink
functions.description: Destructor for UncheckedByteArraySink.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::Append
functions.description: Appends data[0..n-1] to the destination array without performing bound checks.
requirements: data must point to at least n bytes.
The destination buffer must have at least n bytes of remaining capacity; the sink does not check bounds.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::GetAppendBuffer
functions.description: Returns a writable buffer for appending. For this sink, the buffer will typically be the internal destination pointer. Valid until the next operation. After writing at most len bytes, the caller must call Append() with the same pointer and the number of bytes written. If a non-scratch buffer is returned, only a prefix may be passed to Append.
requirements: scratch must point to a caller-owned buffer of at least len bytes if used.
Caller must write no more than len bytes to the returned buffer.
Caller must call Append(returned_pointer, bytes_written) with bytes_written <= len before any other Sink operation.
If a non-scratch buffer is returned, the caller may only pass a prefix of that buffer to Append (must not pass an interior pointer).
Returned buffer becomes invalid after the next operation on this Sink.
The destination buffer must have sufficient remaining capacity; no bound checks are performed.

functions.signature: char* snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::GetAppendBufferVariable(size_t min_size, size_t desired_size_hint, char* scratch, size_t scratch_size, size_t* allocated_size)
functions.description: Returns a writable buffer for appending and writes its capacity to *allocated_size (>= min_size). Valid until the next operation. After writing at most *allocated_size bytes, the caller must call Append() with the same pointer and the number of bytes written. If a non-scratch buffer is returned, only a prefix may be passed to Append.
requirements: scratch must have scratch_size >= min_size if used.
allocated_size must be non-null and writable; on return, *allocated_size >= min_size.
Caller must write no more than *allocated_size bytes to the returned buffer.
Caller must call Append(returned_pointer, bytes_written) with bytes_written <= *allocated_size before any other Sink operation.
If a non-scratch buffer is returned, the caller may only pass a prefix of that buffer to Append (must not pass an interior pointer).
Returned buffer becomes invalid after the next operation on this Sink.
The destination buffer must have sufficient remaining capacity; no bound checks are performed.
desired_size_hint may be 0 if the caller cannot provide a reasonable guess.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::AppendAndTakeOwnership
functions.signature: void snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::AppendAndTakeOwnership(char* bytes, size_t n, void (*deleter)(void*, const char*, size_t), void* deleter_arg)
functions.description: Appends bytes[0..n-1] to the destination without bound checks, taking ownership of the buffer and freeing it via deleter(deleter_arg, bytes, n).
requirements: deleter must be non-null.
bytes must point to a buffer of at least n bytes that can be released using the provided deleter.
Ownership of bytes transfers to the sink; the caller must not read or free bytes after calling this function.
The destination buffer must have sufficient remaining capacity; no bound checks are performed.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::CurrentDestination
functions.description: Returns the current output pointer so a caller can determine how many bytes have been produced (by comparing against the start pointer it supplied). Not part of the Sink interface.

functions.name: snappy::Compress
functions.description: Reads uncompressed bytes from reader and writes the compressed stream to writer, returning the number of bytes written. Intended for streaming I/O using Snappy’s Source/Sink abstractions. Preserves ABI as the basic overload without options.
requirements: reader must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
writer must be a valid, writable snappy::Sink.
On success the return value is the number of compressed bytes appended to writer; callers should not assume any minimum compression ratio.
reader will be consumed as needed; if the same data must be reused, arrange for rewinding or recreating the Source.

functions.name: snappy::Compress
functions.signature: size_t snappy::Compress(snappy::Source* reader, snappy::Sink* writer, snappy::CompressionOptions options);
functions.description: Same as the Source/Sink overload above, but allows selecting compression options (e.g., compression level). Returns the number of bytes written to writer.
requirements: reader must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
writer must be a valid, writable snappy::Sink.
options.level should be within the supported range [snappy::CompressionOptions::MinCompressionLevel(), snappy::CompressionOptions::MaxCompressionLevel()] (currently 1–2).
reader will be consumed as needed; if the same data must be reused, arrange for rewinding or recreating the Source.

functions.name: snappy::GetUncompressedLength
functions.description: Parses the header of a compressed stream from source and writes the uncompressed length to *result. The true length could deviate (e.g., if the stream is truncated). Leaves source in a state unsuitable for further operations; callers must rewind or recreate the Source before further use.
requirements: source must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
result must be a non-null pointer to uint32_t for receiving the length.
After calling, source is not suitable for subsequent operations without rewinding or recreating it (as documented).
Caller must check the boolean return value; false indicates failure to read/parse the length.

functions.name: snappy::GetUncompressedLength
functions.signature: bool snappy::GetUncompressedLength(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, size_t* result);
functions.description: Parses compressed[0..compressed_length-1] (produced by RawCompress/Compress) and stores the uncompressed length in *result. Runs in O(1) time. Returns false on parsing error.
requirements: compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes.
result must be a non-null pointer to size_t for receiving the length.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect parsing errors.
The buffer must have been produced by snappy::RawCompress() or snappy::Compress().

functions.name: snappy::CompressFromIOVec
functions.signature: size_t snappy::CompressFromIOVec(const struct iovec* iov, size_t iov_cnt, std::string* compressed);
functions.description: Compresses the concatenation of iov[0..iov_cnt-1] and replaces *compressed with the compressed data. Returns the number of bytes written. This overload precomputes the total uncompressed length by summing iov[i].iov_len.
requirements: iov must point to an array of at least iov_cnt elements; each iovec must reference readable memory of length iov_len.
compressed must be a valid pointer to a std::string.
On return, *compressed is replaced with the compressed output.
This function preprocesses inputs to compute the total length; if that is undesirable, use RawCompressFromIOVec instead.

functions.name: snappy::CompressFromIOVec
functions.signature: size_t snappy::CompressFromIOVec(const struct iovec* iov, size_t iov_cnt, std::string* compressed, snappy::CompressionOptions options);
functions.description: Same as the iovec overload above but allows passing compression options (e.g., compression level). Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: iov must point to an array of at least iov_cnt elements; each iovec must reference readable memory of length iov_len.
compressed must be a valid pointer to a std::string.
options.level should be within [snappy::CompressionOptions::MinCompressionLevel(), snappy::CompressionOptions::MaxCompressionLevel()] (currently 1–2).
This function preprocesses inputs to compute the total length; if that is undesirable, use RawCompressFromIOVec instead.

functions.name: snappy::Uncompress
functions.signature: bool snappy::Uncompress(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, std::string* uncompressed);
functions.description: Decompresses compressed[0..compressed_length-1] into *uncompressed. Returns false if the input is corrupted and cannot be decompressed. On success, *uncompressed is replaced with the decompressed data.
requirements: uncompressed must be a valid pointer to a std::string.
compressed and *uncompressed must not alias (REQUIRES).
compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/failure.

functions.name: snappy::Uncompress
functions.description: Decompresses from the given compressed Source into the uncompressed Sink. Returns false if the input is corrupted and cannot be decompressed.
requirements: compressed must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
uncompressed must be a valid, writable snappy::Sink.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/failure.
On success, the implementation may consume all data from compressed; if the Source needs to be reused, be prepared to rewind/reset it externally.

functions.name: snappy::UncompressAsMuchAsPossible
functions.description: Attempts to decompress as much as possible from compressed into uncompressed. Returns the number of valid bytes added to the sink. Extra invalid bytes may be emitted due to errors; callers should ignore those. Output is typically the full uncompressed length but may be shorter if an error occurs.
requirements: compressed must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
uncompressed must be a valid, writable snappy::Sink.
Caller must treat the return value as the count of valid bytes and ignore any excess data written to the sink due to errors.
The Source may be consumed up to where decompression failed; prepare to reset/rewind if needed.

functions.name: snappy::RawCompress
functions.signature: void snappy::RawCompress(const char* input, size_t input_length, char* compressed, size_t* compressed_length);
functions.description: Low-level API that compresses input[0..input_length-1] into the provided output buffer. Writes the compressed size to *compressed_length. Caller manages output buffer allocation.
requirements: compressed must point to a writable buffer of at least snappy::MaxCompressedLength(input_length) bytes (REQUIRES).
compressed_length must be a non-null pointer to size_t for receiving the output size.
input must point to at least input_length readable bytes.

functions.name: snappy::RawCompress
functions.signature: void snappy::RawCompress(const char* input, size_t input_length, char* compressed, size_t* compressed_length, snappy::CompressionOptions options);
functions.description: Same as the RawCompress overload above but accepts compression options (e.g., compression level). Writes the compressed size to *compressed_length.
requirements: compressed must point to a writable buffer of at least snappy::MaxCompressedLength(input_length) bytes (REQUIRES).
compressed_length must be a non-null pointer to size_t for receiving the output size.
input must point to at least input_length readable bytes.
options.level should be within [snappy::CompressionOptions::MinCompressionLevel(), snappy::CompressionOptions::MaxCompressionLevel()] (currently 1–2).

functions.name: snappy::RawCompressFromIOVec
functions.signature: void snappy::RawCompressFromIOVec(const struct iovec* iov, size_t uncompressed_length, char* compressed, size_t* compressed_length);
functions.description: Low-level API that compresses the concatenation of iov elements. uncompressed_length is the total number of bytes to read from the iovec array (not the element count). Writes compressed data into compressed and the size to *compressed_length.
requirements: iov must point to a valid array of iovec elements whose concatenated data contains at least uncompressed_length bytes.
uncompressed_length is the total number of bytes to be read from the iovec elements (not the number of elements).
compressed must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the worst-case size (at least snappy::MaxCompressedLength(uncompressed_length) is recommended).
compressed_length must be a non-null pointer to size_t for receiving the output size.

functions.name: snappy::RawCompressFromIOVec
functions.signature: void snappy::RawCompressFromIOVec(const struct iovec* iov, size_t uncompressed_length, char* compressed, size_t* compressed_length, snappy::CompressionOptions options);
functions.description: Same as the RawCompressFromIOVec overload above but accepts compression options (e.g., compression level).
requirements: iov must point to a valid array of iovec elements whose concatenated data contains at least uncompressed_length bytes.
uncompressed_length is the total number of bytes to be read from the iovec elements (not the number of elements).
compressed must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the worst-case size (at least snappy::MaxCompressedLength(uncompressed_length) is recommended).
compressed_length must be a non-null pointer to size_t for receiving the output size.
options.level should be within [snappy::CompressionOptions::MinCompressionLevel(), snappy::CompressionOptions::MaxCompressionLevel()] (currently 1–2).

functions.name: snappy::RawUncompress
functions.signature: bool snappy::RawUncompress(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, char* uncompressed);
functions.description: Low-level API that decompresses compressed[0..compressed_length-1] into the caller-provided uncompressed buffer, which must be large enough for the entire output. Returns false if the input is corrupted and cannot be decompressed.
requirements: compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes.
uncompressed must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the full uncompressed output (typically obtained via GetUncompressedLength).
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/failure.

functions.name: snappy::RawUncompress
functions.description: Low-level API that decompresses from a Source into the caller-provided uncompressed buffer (which must be large enough). Returns false if the input is corrupted and cannot be decompressed.
requirements: compressed must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
uncompressed must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the entire uncompressed output (typically determined via GetUncompressedLength).
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/failure.

functions.name: snappy::RawUncompressToIOVec
functions.signature: bool snappy::RawUncompressToIOVec(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, const struct iovec* iov, size_t iov_cnt);
functions.description: Decompresses compressed[0..compressed_length-1] and scatters the uncompressed bytes across the iovec array. Returns false if the input is corrupted and cannot be decompressed.
requirements: iov must point to an array of at least iov_cnt elements.
The cumulative size of the iovec buffers must be at least the full uncompressed size of the stream (typically GetUncompressedLength).
The individual buffers in iov must not overlap with each other.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/failure.
compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes.

functions.name: snappy::RawUncompressToIOVec
functions.signature: bool snappy::RawUncompressToIOVec(snappy::Source* compressed, const struct iovec* iov, size_t iov_cnt);
functions.description: Decompresses from a Source and scatters the uncompressed bytes across the provided iovec array. Returns false if the input is corrupted and cannot be decompressed.
requirements: compressed must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
iov must point to an array of at least iov_cnt elements.
The cumulative size of the iovec buffers must be at least the full uncompressed size of the stream (typically GetUncompressedLength).
The individual buffers in iov must not overlap with each other.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/failure.

functions.name: snappy::MaxCompressedLength
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of bytes that Snappy could produce when compressing source_bytes of input. Use this to size output buffers for RawCompress-style APIs.
requirements: source_bytes should reflect the actual uncompressed input size to ensure the returned bound is sufficient for allocation.

functions.name: snappy::IsValidCompressedBuffer
functions.signature: bool snappy::IsValidCompressedBuffer(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length);
functions.description: Returns true iff the contents of compressed[0..compressed_length-1] can be successfully decompressed. Does not return the uncompressed data. Typically at least 4× faster than actual decompression.
requirements: compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes.
Caller should not expect any output—this only validates.
Time cost is proportional to compressed_length.

functions.name: snappy::IsValidCompressed
functions.description: Returns true iff the contents of the compressed Source can be successfully decompressed. Does not return the uncompressed data. Typically at least 4× faster than actual decompression. On success, consumes all of the Source; on failure, consumes an unspecified prefix.
requirements: compressed must be a valid, readable snappy::Source.
On success the entire Source is consumed; on failure an unspecified prefix is consumed—callers that need to reuse the Source must arrange to clone/reset/rewind it beforehand.
This function produces no output; it only validates the stream.

functions.name: snappy_compress
functions.signature: snappy_status snappy_compress(const char* input, size_t input_length, char* compressed, size_t* compressed_length);
functions.description: Compresses input[0..input_length-1] into the buffer compressed, using Snappy. The caller must set *compressed_length to the available space in compressed before the call; on success, it is updated to the actual compressed size and SNAPPY_OK is returned. If the provided buffer is too small (less than snappy_max_compressed_length(input_length)), the function returns SNAPPY_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL. Intended for fast, general-purpose compression where the output buffer is caller-managed.
requirements: input must point to at least input_length readable bytes.
compressed must point to a writable buffer whose size is provided in *compressed_length prior to the call.
*compressed_length must be initialized by the caller to the available size of compressed.
For successful compression, the available size in compressed must be at least snappy_max_compressed_length(input_length); otherwise the function returns SNAPPY_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL.
compressed_length must be a valid, non-null pointer; on success it will be updated to the exact number of bytes written.
Function returns SNAPPY_OK on success; callers should check the return value for SNAPPY_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL or other errors.

functions.name: snappy_uncompress
functions.signature: snappy_status snappy_uncompress(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, char* uncompressed, size_t* uncompressed_length);
functions.description: Decompresses a buffer produced by snappy_compress. Reads compressed[0..compressed_length-1] and writes the uncompressed data into uncompressed, up to the size provided via *uncompressed_length. On success, writes the exact decompressed size to *uncompressed_length and returns SNAPPY_OK. If the compressed data is invalid/corrupted, returns a failure status (not SNAPPY_OK, e.g., SNAPPY_INVALID_INPUT). If the destination buffer is too small (less than the size reported by snappy_uncompressed_length for this stream), returns SNAPPY_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL.
requirements: compressed must point to a buffer of length compressed_length bytes that was produced by snappy_compress().
uncompressed must point to a writable buffer with at least the capacity specified by *uncompressed_length on entry.

Before calling, the caller must either size the output buffer to at least the length returned by snappy_uncompressed_length(compressed, compressed_length, &len) or be prepared to handle SNAPPY_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL.
uncompressed_length must be a valid, non-null pointer; on entry it must contain the available capacity; on success it is updated to the actual decompressed size.
Callers must check the return value for SNAPPY_OK, SNAPPY_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, or invalid input errors before using the output.

functions.name: snappy_max_compressed_length
functions.description: Returns the maximum possible size of the compressed representation of an input buffer of length source_length. Use this to allocate a sufficiently large destination buffer before calling snappy_compress.
requirements: source_length must be the exact size (in bytes) of the input that will be compressed.
The return value can be used as an upper bound for the compressed buffer size when calling snappy_compress.

functions.name: snappy_uncompressed_length
functions.signature: snappy_status snappy_uncompressed_length(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, size_t* result);
functions.description: Returns (in *result) the length of the data that would be produced by decompressing the given compressed buffer, assuming it was created by snappy_compress. Runs in O(1) time. Returns SNAPPY_OK on success, or SNAPPY_INVALID_INPUT if the compressed stream cannot be parsed.
requirements: compressed must point to data that was produced by snappy_compress().
compressed_length must be the exact size in bytes of the compressed data.
result must be a valid, non-null pointer where the uncompressed length will be stored on success.
Callers must check the return value for SNAPPY_OK or SNAPPY_INVALID_INPUT before using *result.

functions.name: snappy_validate_compressed_buffer
functions.signature: snappy_status snappy_validate_compressed_buffer(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length);
functions.description: Validates whether the given compressed buffer can be successfully decompressed. Does not produce the uncompressed data. Returns SNAPPY_OK if valid, otherwise SNAPPY_INVALID_INPUT. Typically runs in time proportional to compressed_length and is usually at least 4x faster than full decompression.
requirements: compressed must point to compressed_length readable bytes.
compressed_length must be the size in bytes of the compressed buffer to validate.
Callers must check the return value for SNAPPY_OK or SNAPPY_INVALID_INPUT before proceeding (e.g., before allocating and decompressing).

import random
import struct
import zlib

# Although the target is Snappy, we cannot import snappy. We therefore craft
# uncompressed payloads that, when the harness chooses to compress using the
# library under test, will exercise diverse behaviors. For negative paths, the
# harness already feeds random bytes. Our job is to provide bytes that are good
# uncompressed payload candidates and sometimes already-compressed data patterns
# that are known to compress well or poorly, include edge cases, etc.
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the harness is fed our single returned bytes buffer. The
# harness often uses that buffer as the uncompressed payload which it then
# compresses using snappy::RawCompress. Therefore we focus on generating a wide
# variety of uncompressed inputs that are interesting for Snappy:
# - Highly repetitive runs (good compression)
# - Slightly noisy repetitions (match finding, copy literals)
# - Small inputs (including empty)
# - Inputs around internal block boundaries (Snappy uses 32KB window; we cap
#   sizes per harness to <=1500, but we still vary sizes and patterns)
# - ASCII text, UTF-8, binary, zero bytes, incremental bytes, random bytes
# - Mixtures of segments to trigger both literal and copy emissions
#
# The result must be <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_OUT = 4096

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = (b" \t\n\r" +
                b"0123456789" +
                b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" +
                b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" +
                b".,;:-_!?/\\'\"()[]{}<>@#$%^&*+=|")
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _repetitive(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n == 0:
        return b""
    token_len = rng.randint(1, min(32, max(1, n)))
    token = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(token_len))
    return (token * (n // token_len + 1))[:n]

def _sliding_repeats(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n == 0:
        return b""
    base = bytearray(_repetitive(rng, max(16, n // 4)))
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        # Copy a windowed slice with some mutations
        start = rng.randint(0, max(0, len(base) - 1))
        length = rng.randint(8, 64)
        chunk = bytes(base[start:start+length])
        if not chunk:
            chunk = bytes([rng.getrandbits(8)])
        # Randomly flip a few bytes to create near-matches
        b = bytearray(chunk)
        flips = rng.randint(0, max(1, len(b)//16))
        for _ in range(flips):
            idx = rng.randrange(len(b))
            b[idx] ^= 1 << rng.randrange(8)
        out.extend(b)
    return bytes(out[:n])

def _incrementing(n: int, start: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(n))

def _zeros(n: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00" * n

def _ones(n: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\xFF" * n

def _utf8_text(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Build plausible UTF-8 by mixing ASCII and some multi-byte sequences
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.75:
            out.append(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E))  # printable ASCII
        elif choice < 0.9:
            # 2-byte sequence
            cp = rng.randint(0x80, 0x7FF)
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            # 3-byte sequence
            cp = rng.randint(0x800, 0xFFFF)
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0x20
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
    return bytes(out[:n])

def _mix_segments(rng: random.Random, total: int) -> bytes:
    makers = [
        lambda m: _zeros(m),
        lambda m: _ones(m),
        lambda m: _incrementing(m, rng.randrange(256)),
        lambda m: _repetitive(rng, m),
        lambda m: _sliding_repeats(rng, m),
        lambda m: _rand_ascii(rng, m),
        lambda m: _utf8_text(rng, m),
        lambda m: rng.randbytes(m) if m > 0 else b"",
    ]
    parts = []
    remaining = total
    # Aim for 3-10 segments
    segs = rng.randint(3, 10)
    for i in range(segs):
        if i == segs - 1:
            m = remaining
        else:
            m = rng.randint(0, remaining)
        parts.append(rng.choice(makers)(m))
        remaining -= m
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
    # Occasionally duplicate previous data to create back-references
    if parts and rng.random() < 0.6:
        dup_src = b"".join(parts)
        if dup_src:
            rep_len = rng.randint(1, min(128, len(dup_src)))
            rep_off = rng.randint(0, max(0, len(dup_src) - rep_len))
            parts.append(dup_src[rep_off:rep_off+rep_len] * rng.randint(1, 8))
    out = b"".join(parts)[:total]
    return out

def _around_sizes(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Harness caps to <=1500 for many paths; choose diverse sizes including 0.
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024, 1500]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    return rng.randint(0, 1500)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide an overall strategy
    strat = rng.random()
    size = _around_sizes(rng)

    if strat < 0.1:
        data = _zeros(size)
    elif strat < 0.2:
        data = _ones(size)
    elif strat < 0.32:
        data = _incrementing(size, rng.randrange(256))
    elif strat < 0.45:
        data = _repetitive(rng, size)
    elif strat < 0.6:
        data = _sliding_repeats(rng, size)
    elif strat < 0.75:
        data = _rand_ascii(rng, size)
    elif strat < 0.9:
        data = _utf8_text(rng, size)
    else:
        data = _mix_segments(rng, size)

    # Occasionally prefix with known file headers or structured patterns that
    # may influence compression ratios and parsing behaviors when treated as raw bytes.
    if data and rng.random() < 0.25:
        headers = [
            b"\x1F\x8B\x08\x00",  # gzip magic + method/flags
            b"PK\x03\x04",          # ZIP local header magic
            b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1A\n", # PNG signature
            b"%PDF-",                # PDF header
            b"{\n\t\"k\": ",         # JSON-like start
        ]
        h = rng.choice(headers)
        remain = max(0, MAX_OUT - len(h))
        data = (h + data)[:min(len(h) + len(data), remain)]

    # Ensure cap
    return bytes(data[:MAX_OUT])
